items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: On the corner at 125th and 8th, upstairs, was Daddy Grace’s church. And the windows were always open. Now they had saxophone, drum, trombone, guitar, tambourine.

ctx.x: As long as you didn’t pick that one foot up over the other and cross it, then they wouldn’t —

Right, and it says, make the joyful noise unto the Lord. The many times that I used to play the Apollo Theater, the most urgent thing that would happen when the show was over, everybody would come out the stage entrance which was on 126th Street, come around the block to 8th Avenue, past the Braddock Bar and cross the street. On the corner at 125th and 8th, upstairs, was Daddy Grace’s church. And the windows were always open. Now they had saxophone, drum, trombone, guitar, tambourine. If you wanted to hear music,…
And the tambourines with their heads on them right?
